question_text: 25. RESCUE BOAT & LAUNCHING ARRANGEMENT
guidance: Rescue boats stowed for launching in < 5 minutes & have 2 release capabilities, one off-load & one on-load, or only one if rescue boat can only be released when waterborne. The on-load release to be protected against accidental or premature use (i.e. on-load operation of release mechanism shall require a sustained action by the operator). To prevent an accidental release, the mechanical protection (interlock) should only engage when the release mechanism is completely set. Instructions provided with a warning notice. Where a single fall or hook system is used for launching, a single capability to release the rescue boat only when it is waterborne is adequate

38. NUMBER & POSITION
guidance: One P&S covering complete crew plus one for 6 persons fwd, if length from accommodation to fcle>100m. One or more inflatable or rigid liferafts stowed for easy side-to-side transfer at a single open deck level for total number of persons. If not stowed in a position like this, the total capacity available on each side shall be for total number of persons. If a free-fall lifeboat is fitted, ships shall have one or more inflatable or rigid liferafts, on each side for the total number of persons. The liferafts on at least one side shall have launching appliances. For davit launched liferafts, the launching appliances include an automatic release hook to prevent premature release during lowering & release the liferaft when waterborne. The release hook to include a capability to release the hook under load. The on-load release control shall: a. Be differentiated from the control which activates the automatic release; b. Require at least two separate actions to operate; c. Be designed such that crew members on deck can observe when the release mechanism is properly and completely set

question_text: 51. CHECK THE PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENT REQUIRED BY THE IBC OR BCH CODES
guidance: PPE consisting of large aprons, special gloves with long sleeves, suitable footwear, coveralls of chemical-resistant material & tight-fitting goggles or face shields or both. The PPE shall cover all skin so that no part of body is unprotected. Work clothes & PPE kept in easily accessible places & in special lockers - not within accommodation spaces, with the exception of new, unused equipment & equipment not used since undergoing a thorough cleaning process. The Administration may, however, approve storage rooms in accommodation spaces if adequately segregated from living spaces.

question_text: 52. SAFETY EQUIPMENT CORRECTLY LOCATED & EXAMINED BY AN EXPERT AGENCY ANNUALLY.
guidance: An ‘expert’ may be a member of the crew provided they have attended relevant courses and have documentation available to prove it. Ships shall have>3 complete sets of safety equipment, each permitting personnel to enter a gas-filled compartment & work there for > 20 minutes. One complete set consists of 1 SCBA (not using stored oxygen), protective clothing, boots, gloves & tight-fitting goggles, fireproof line with belt resistant to cargoes carried & explosion-proof lamp. All ships carry either 1 set of fully charged spare air bottles for each BA, a special air compressor for supply of high-pressure air of the required purity & a charging manifold capable of dealing with sufficient spare air bottles for the BA or fully charged spare air bottles with a total free air capacity>6,000 l for each BA on board in excess of SOLAS requirements. For vessels carrying toxic cargoes, the safety equipment should provide full protection. The suits capable of providing adequate protection against the product & fitted with integral gloves & boots. Such suits are not required if vessel not carry toxic cargoes. At least 1 set of safety equipment kept in marked locker in a readily accessible place near cargo pump room. The other sets also kept in suitable, marked, easily accessible places.

question_text: 53. USE OF FILTER-TYPE RESPIRATORS / CANISTER MASKS PROHIBITED AND ARE THERE ADEQUATE CONTROLS FOR ENFORCING THIS PROHIBITION.
guidance: Use of filter type respirators, canister masks etc is absolutely prohibited as per clear Company’s Policy. Where filter-type respirators exist onboard, these are not to be considered as part of the safety equipment required by the Codes. Their use is strictly forbidden, their access decontrolled and they should be kept locked under the personal custody of the Master Only BA is approved as respiratory protection means.

question_text: 19. SUCTION VALVES TIGHTNESS MONITORING & TESTING ARRANGEMENTS
guidance: A pressure / vacuum gauge & air quick coupling between outboard & inboard valves for testing. Devices fitted so that readings can be taken high enough from P/R lower platform, to avoid exposure to P/R vapours. Test pressure<3.5 bar. A device should be installed to monitor pressure build-up and determine liquid make-up in the section of pipeline which lies between inboard and outboard sea valves. Such a device would both provide an early indication of leakage through either valve during cargo operations and enable the leaking valve to be identified. During cargo operations pressure build-up in this line would be apparent from the gauge reading and would indicate that one of the valves was leaking. The use of a pressure/vacuum gauge, rather than a pressure-only gauge, is preferable in that it will provide a reliable indication of a vacuum in the line prior to opening the sea valve for ballasting

guidance: High-level alarm system independent of both the gauging devices and the overflow-control alarm. On a Chemical tanker, “closed” loading is required at all times. In such cases, use of portable UTI tapes is not permitted.

15. A volatile product is petroleum having a flash point <60C. If a cargo is being handled at a temperature within 100C of its flashpoint, it should be considered volatile. Therefore, a cargo with a flashpoint of 80C is considered volatile if handled at a temperature of 70C or above.)

question_text: 66. VENTILATION OF P/R SPACES
guidance: Mechanically ventilated & discharges from exhaust fans led to safe place on deck. Changes of air>20 per hour. The vent. shall be of suction type using fans of non-sparking type. On vessels constructed after 1/7/2002 the air ducts arranged so that all space is effectively ventilated. On some older vessels the vent. system operates with one fan on supply & the other on extraction. Nevertheless, there should be extraction from both sides of P/R bilge area. Lighting, except em. lighting, interlocked with vent. such that the vent. shall be in operation when switching on the lighting. Failure of vent. shall not cause the lighting to go out. If only one extraction fan, there should be alternative arrangements to re-establish extraction in case of failure, i.e. a spare motor, or the ability to reverse the polarity of a supply fan

question_text: 67. CARGO SAMPLE LOCKER SITUATED WITHIN THE MAIN CARGO AREA, IN ORDER, ADEQUATELY VENTILATED & SUITABLY CONSTRUCTED TO PREVENT BREAKAGES (Only if locker contains flammable liquids, are SOLAS fire extinguishing arrangements required. The stowage space should be:
68. Cell divided in order to avoid shifting of the bottles at sea;

72. INDIVIDUAL P/V VALVES: Date of last calibration: ………………….
guidance: In order, inspected & cleaned regularly. High jet cones & flaps should not be jacked open, particularly when loading. High jet vents not fitted with flame screens & their correct operation relies on a pressure build-up within the compartment which opens the valve at a predetermined level & results in a gas exit velocity>30 m/sec. This result in protection against passage of flame, the speed of which is 7.5 m/sec. Request the manual lifting of P/V valves. P/V valves checked for free movement prior to the commencement of each cargo operation as required by the Ship to Shore Safety check list. Condition inspection, last overhaul and regular maintenance records, setting, test, Class attestation, vacuum side fitted with flame screen in good condition

question_text: 77. VENTING SYSTEM AS PER SOLAS SECONDARY VENTING ARRANGEMENT REQUIREMENTS
guidance: A secondary means of full flow relief of vapour, air or IG mixtures shall be provided. Alternatively, pressure sensors may be fitted in each tank protected by the primary venting arrangement with a monitoring system in CCR or position from which cargo operations are carried out. Such monitoring equipment shall also provide an alarm which is activated by detection of over-pressure or under-pressure conditions within a tank. The IBC Code requires: Controlled tank venting systems should consist of a primary and a secondary means of allowing full flow relief of vapour to prevent over-pressure or under-pressure in the event of failure of one means

The oxygen content of IG in IG supply mains on discharge side of the gas blowers. c. The devices placed in CCR or in a position accessible to the Officer in charge of cargo operations. Meters shall also be fitted: a. In the bridge to indicate at all times the pressure of the IG main forward of the non-return devices; b. In the machinery control room or in the machinery space to indicate the oxygen content of the IG in IG supply mains on the discharge side of the gas blowers

question_text: 88. OXYGEN CONTENT OF IG DELIVERY AT OR BELOW THE PERMITTED MAXIMUM
guidance: Record if the oxygen delivery is more than 5% or if a high oxygen level alarm is not fitted. For tankers constructed after 1/9/84: The system capable of maintaining the atmosphere in any part of any cargo tank with oxygen> 8% by volume and at a positive pressure at all times in port and at sea, except when it is necessary for the tank to be gas free. System capable of delivering IG with oxygen< 5% by volume in IG supply main to the cargo tanks. guidance: In order, operating effectively, ready for use. Anchor securing arrangements (cable stoppers etc.), shackle marks, securing chains, devil ’s claw, Smit type bracket & mooring chain, indication of shackles paid out. question_text: 8. HYDRAULIC BOW STOPPER (Safeguards to prevent accidental release).
9. MOORING ROPES & WIRES
guidance: Inspect wear condition, Certificates, inspection records. Check correct reeling on drums and stowage in stores. Polypropylene ropes are not recommended. If used, tails shall be made of a material with a high breaking strength such as braided or plaited nylon, or high modulus synthetic fibre rope. The size of rope shall ensure that the tail has a dry breaking strength>125% of associated wire. Nylon tails should have strength>137% than the associated wire to allow for the reduction in wet strength. Mooring ropes & wires leading to the same direction not mixed, always of the same material & length

question_text: 10. MOORINGS SATISFACTORILY DEPLOYED & TENDED. MOORING LINES SECURED TO BITTS & TURNED UP CORRECTLY TO WINCH DRUMS
guidance: The recommended method of turning a rope up on bitts is to take 1-2 full turns around the leading post before ‘figure-of-eighting’. The reason for this is to reduce the tendency to pull the two posts together. Mooring lines must not be secured to winch warping drums

question_text: 11. ALL POWERED MOORING LINES: 1. Secured on brakes and the winches are out of gear. 2.Correctly reeled on drums.
guidance: A band brake is designed to work in one direction only, so the line must always be reeled correctly on drum. The line is properly reeled if it is pulling against the fixed end of the brake strap. Disc brakes work equally well in either direction

question_text: 12. MOORING FITTINGS, BITTS, BOLLARDS, CHOCKS, PEDESTAL ROLLERS, CLOSED CHOCKS, UNIVERSAL ROLLER LEADS, CHAIN STOPPERS & MOORING WINCHES

question_text: 13. MOORING TAILS
guidance: Wear condition, correct fitting of connecting links. Tails replaced every 18 months

question_text: 14. ON SPLIT DRUM WINCHES ALL LINES MADE FAST WITH NO MORE THAN ONE LAYER ON EACH TENSION SIDE OF DRUM
guidance: More than one layer increases the effective lever and reduces the brake holding capacity

question_text: 15. MOORING LINES STOWED NEATLY TO MINIMISE TRIPPING HAZARDS AND MOORING AREAS CLEAR AND UNOBSTRUCTED

question_text: 18. IF MOORING TAILS ARE FITTED TO WIRES, DO THEY HAVE PROPER CONNECTING LINKS & ARE THEY CORRECTLY FITTED?
guidance: Connecting links are Tonsberg, Mandal or Boss shackles. Tonsberg have a straight pin and the tail should be connected to it. Mandal has a curved roller and the wire should be connected to it. Boss shackles are available in both versions

question_text: 19. EMERGENCY TOWING-OFF WIRES (FIRE WIRES) OF APPROPRIATE SIZE, IN SATISFACTORY CONDITION & CONFORM TO OCIMF RECOMMENDATIONS
guidance: Fire wires should be steel wire lines of 6 x 36 construction. Use of synthetic or natural fibre ropes is not permitted. The recommended sizes of fire wires are: a. Less than 20,000 dwt: 30 tonnes MBL, 25 m in length; b. 20,000 – 100,000 dwt: 50 tonnes MBL, 45 m in length; c. 100,000 – 300,000 dwt: 90 tonnes MBL, 60 m in length; d. 300,000 + dwt 110 tonnes MBL, 70 m in length

question_text: 20. EMERGENCY TOWING ARRANGEMENTS (ETA) (Available for deployment fwd & aft. Condition, maintenance records, Class approved, Review of line handling procedures -passing and receiving messenger lines, towlines, bridles- and of the layout structural adequacy and safe working loads of connection points fairleads chocks, winches, bitts, bollards. For tankers constructed on or after 1/7/02: Arrangements capable of rapid deployment in absence of main power on ship to be towed and easy connection to towing ship. At least one ETA pre-rigged ready for deployment, and ETAs at both ends of adequate strength. For tankers constructed before 1/7/02: Design & construction approved by administration. The aft ETA to be pre-rigged/capable of deployed by 1 person in 15 minutes. The fwd ETA capable of deployed in 1 hour. It is unlikely that a length of chain could be retrieved within the time limit if stored in F’cle. Fwd ETAs which comply with requirements for aft ETAs are accepted. All ETAs marked to facilitate use in darkness. All em. towing components regularly inspected by crew. Once the system has been deployed the watertight integrity of adjacent spaces to be maintained. The prime ETA may be fitted either fwd or aft.
21. PEDESTAL FAIRLEADS, ROLLER FAIRLEADS AND OTHER ROLLERS WELL GREASED AND FREE TO TURN. BITTS AND CHOCKS ARE FREE OF GROOVING
guidance: winch drums, chocks and fairleads must be smooth and free of rust and paint when using fibre ropes to avoid abrasion; roller leads should be kept lubricated and freely moving

question_text: 22. IS SINGLE POINT MOORING (SPM) AND ASSOCIATED EQUIPMENT FITTED TO OCIMF RECOMMENDATIONS? Ships trading to SPM’s shall be equipped with bow chain stoppers designed to accept 76 mm chafe chain: a) Up to 150,000 tdw: 1 stopper 200 tonnes swl b) 150 to 350,000 tdw: 2 stoppers 200 tonnes swl c) Over 350,000 tdw: 2 stoppers 250 tonnes swl Stoppers shall be located 2.7-3.7 m inboard from bow fairlead and consideration should be given to the correct alignment of stoppers relative to the lead between bow fairlead, stopper, pedestal fairlead and winch drum or the warping drum of winch. A bow fairlead should measure at least 600 by 450 mm and be placed on the centre line. Two fairleads are recommended for ships over 150,000 tonnes dwt., spaced 2 m. centre to centre apart, but in no case more than 3 m).

23. IF THE VESSEL IS EQUIPPED FOR MOORING AT SPM, CAN THE PICK-UP CAN THE PICK-UP HAWSER BE LED TO A WINCH STORAGE DRUM RATHER THAN THE WARPING DRUM END AND WITHOUT USE OF ONE OR MORE PEDESTAL FAIRLEADS INVOLVING AN ACUTE ANGLE OF LEAD?
guidance: If the arrangement requires use of more than one pedestal roller to lead the hawser to winch storage drum, comment as to arrangement provided. Many SBM terminals require a (nearly) direct lead from bow fairlead through the bow stopper and either directly to a winch storage drum or round a single pedestal fairlead at a shallow angle to a winch storage drum. If a pedestal fairlead is utilised, it should be located>4.5 m aft of aft side of bow stopper and provide a (nearly) direct, lead to storage drum. Use of more than one pedestal fairlead, or if the angle of lead is excessive, may cause excess load to pedestal fairlead. If a winch storage drum is used to stow the pick-up rope, it shall be of sufficient size to accommodate 150 m. of 80 mm diam. rope

question_text: 24. IF THE VAPOUR RETURN MANIFOLDS ARE DESIGNED FOR USE AT SBM DO THEY COMPLY WITH REQUIREMENTS? (Vapour return system manifolds (VRSM) which are designed for use at SBM: a) Should be painted red/yellow/red; b) Should be supported to the same strength as the cargo manifolds; c) Hose rails at ship's side should be of the same strength and construction throughout their length, extend beyond the VRSM to permit use at SBMs and fitted with stopper plates at both the fwd & aft ends of hose rail; d) A closed chock should be fitted at the ship's side in line with the VRSM; e) A cruciform bollard should be fitted (nearly) in line with VRSM to allow securing of VRS hose hang-off chain; f) Two deck pad-eyes of size sufficient to secure 16" floating hose should be provided, one to either side of line from the closed chock to VRSM; g) Means to thoroughly drain the VRSM should be provided at the lowest point in VRS line to avoid risk of liquid carry-over into the floating hose).

guidance: All relevant dangerous areas to be properly identified and painted on deck in the vicinity of moorings deployment as per CSWP

question_text: 26. ARE SUFFICIENT CLOSED FAIRLEADS AND MOORING BITTS PROVIDED FOR STS?
guidance: All fairleads used during STS transfer operations should be of an enclosed type, strong enough to take the anticipated mooring loads and large enough to allow the mooring line (plus any soft rope and tackle) to pass through. Full strength enclosed fairleads and bitts for spring lines need to be positioned no more than 35 m fwd & aft of cargo manifold. Tankers fitted with an array of mooring bitts of sufficient strength on each side of the ship. In addition, it is recommended that provision be made for securing fender lines

question_text: 21. 21. ARE LIGHT FITTINGS IN GAS-HAZARDOUS AREAS EX 'D' RATED AND IN A SATISFACTORY CONDITION?
guidance: Lights either explosion-proof or pressurised. The flame paths of explosion-proof lights should not be painted over. Fluorescent fittings will generally have flame paths at each end. The manufacturer’s or administration’s certificate approving the fitting for use in gas-hazardous areas will be invalidated if the correct bolts for securing the cover, or the correct light bulb size, are not used. Attention to the following: a. Cracks in metal, cracked or broken glasses or failure of cement around cemented glasses in flameproof or explosion proof enclosures; b. Covers of flameproof enclosures to ensure that they are tight, that no bolts are missing, and that no gaskets are present between mating metal surfaces; c. Each connection to ensure that it is properly connected; d. Possible slackness of joints in conduit runs and fittings.
